name: Elitism
summary: Elitism holds that political power is, or should be, in the hands of a minority: the normative strand (Plato) says the best qualified ought to rule, and classical elite theory (Mosca, Pareto, Michels) says every society, democracies included, is in fact ruled by an organised minority. Democratic elitism (Salvemini, Schumpeter) accepts that premise and defends competition between elites as what makes a regime democratic.
scope: Normative elitism as stated in Plato's Republic and classical and democratic elite theory as set out by Michels's Political Parties and the Damele and Campos survey of Mosca, Pareto, Michels, Burnham, Salvemini and Schumpeter. Plato's guardian property and family arrangements, and any later association with fascism, race, wealth franchise or hereditary aristocracy, are not part of the profile. Where the normative and descriptive strands say nothing about a statement it is null.
